consistency.observation: Overview and Personal Information share the Personal Harbor frame and account tools even though phone moves sections into a disclosure.

states.observation: The authenticated overview, private identity record, initial phone arrival problem, recovery and Home return are visible in combination.

responsive.observation: Phone fits the fields and record without horizontal overflow, with a vertical orientation problem on deep entry documented in the finding.

keyboard.observation: The capture exercises the account card and Home return and reports keyboard success. The protected-main control also demonstrates heading recovery with the Home key.

focus.observation: Desktop focus is visible on the destination heading, with phone focus visibility impaired at the scrolled arrival and restored at top/Home.

feedback.observation: The page exposes account identity and active-account state without a save confirmation, and the Home heading identifies the return.

motion.observation: The reduced-motion recordings show a direct route change and return; the initial phone scroll position is an orientation issue.

continuity.observation: The same Creator remains signed in during the identity read and returns Home without an account mutation in the exercised path.

complexity.observation: The identity read and optional email mutation controls are visually separated, though the phone arrival makes the latter prominent initially.

role-outcomes.observation: The account owner reaches the real private record and can return through the advertised Home action. Phone orientation needs the observed recovery.

fallbacks.observation: A Home route remains visible from the form viewport and the destination top is recoverable. Auth denials and other lifecycle actions were outside the recording.

findings.observation: At 390×844 the phone starts the Personal Information route at Change primary email after opening the deeply scrolled profile card, with the destination title and identity outside the viewport. The exact candidate recording shows the destination top and identity by approximately 2.45 seconds before authenticated Home return. Protected-main control 00420421bacc6e9b923c5e50852a83a858886131 in run 45181002598 job 137714476061 reproduced the deep-entry issue at three samples (scrollY 712, focused H1 top −589 px). Home key brought the heading into view. The preserved identity read and visible Home return are completed, and this is an existing, recoverable orientation issue. Current-candidate viewport and control log establish the symptom and baseline comparison. Numeric geometry is available for the earlier control only.

composition.observation: The centered parchment auth card keeps one primary task per screen and preserves the accepted Homeport form treatment.

hierarchy.observation: Sign in and Forgot password are dominant distinct headings, with a subordinate Return to Sign In action on the recovery page.

typography.observation: The large serif title and dark compact persistent field labels remain differentiated in both cards.

spacing.observation: Input and primary-button blocks stay in a compact column, with smaller phone margins and no sideways clipping.

controls.observation: The Account menu leads to Sign In, Forgot Password opens recovery, and Return to Sign In restores the original form.

contrast.observation: Dark heading and label text on parchment remain easy to identify, with forms visibly separated from the dark surrounding shell.

consistency.observation: The two routes share a consistent form shell while their title, field set and call to action express different tasks.

states.observation: Sign-in entry, single-email recovery and the returned sign-in form are visible on both device sizes.

responsive.observation: Inputs and actions remain inside the vertical phone card, and the recovery and return controls remain in flow.

keyboard.observation: Capture reports keyboard success for the visible account menu, sign-in, recovery and return controls.

focus.observation: The destination heading visibly receives focus for sign-in, recovery and the return.

feedback.observation: The switch to a recovery-specific heading and labelled send action confirms arrival, and return restores the sign-in title and password field.

motion.observation: Both reduced-motion recordings show direct navigation between authentication cards without delayed access to the destination.

continuity.observation: Returning restores the same authentication form and navigation frame under the anonymous session.

complexity.observation: Recovery keeps a single email field and return link, with the multi-field credential task staying on Sign in.

role-outcomes.observation: An anonymous person reaches canonical login and password recovery from the product gateway and can return without signing in.

fallbacks.observation: The sign-in capture shows provider availability guidance, while the human-visible email/password and recovery paths remain available. Delivery of a reset link was outside this recording.

composition.observation: The Personal Information form keeps the same Account layout through the draft state, and Home is a clearly distinct destination.

hierarchy.observation: Personal Information continues to identify the page, with save and unsaved feedback visually subordinate to that heading.

typography.observation: Form labels and Unsaved changes remain distinct from the serif page heading and the editable display name.

spacing.observation: Desktop retains the section rail, phone stacks sections above the form, and the draft follows the same spacing as the initial form.

controls.observation: The labelled display-name input and Save display name are distinct, with a separate visible Home return.

contrast.observation: The edited text field receives a light outline with readable value against teal, and Home receives a strong destination outline.

consistency.observation: The form, account framing and button style stay consistent before and after editing.

states.observation: Settled editor, visible pending draft and Home return are separately evidenced in both contexts.

responsive.observation: On phone the editable field and its draft state remain within the single-column layout and Home resumes its compact gateway.

keyboard.observation: The capture reports keyboard success; typed input visibly changes the display name without activating Save.

focus.observation: The display-name input has a visible focus indicator and retained value during the pending state, followed by visible destination focus on Home.

feedback.observation: Unsaved changes appears in the actual form while it contains the altered name, so feedback is distinguishable from saved account data.

motion.observation: Captured reduced-mode route and feedback are direct. The capture describes separate browser cases for the live OS preference changes.

continuity.observation: The same Creator's Account form retains the local draft through the visible pending state and the journey returns to authenticated Home.

complexity.observation: One editable field, a labelled save action and an independent route out keep the draft decision clear.

role-outcomes.observation: A Creator can type a local, clearly unsaved change and return to Home without the journey invoking an account save.

fallbacks.observation: Local pending feedback stays visible until leaving, and the Home link remains usable; production Showcase availability is outside this capture.
